newsitem.title: IRAN: Iran women groups denounce Afghan Taleban policies.
newsitem.headline: Iran women groups denounce Afghan Taleban policies.

text.p: Iranian women's groups have denouced as "un-Islamic" restrictions imposed on women by the radical Moslem Taleban militia in neighbouring Afghanistan, a newspaper said on Wednesday.

The daily Kayhan quoted a statement by the non-governmental women's organisations as condemning "the denial of women's human rights in Afghanistan, which has nothing to do with the principles of Islam and the Holy Koran".

"Under Islamic teachings, women enjoy a high and special status and have social, cultural, political and economic rights. It is therefore amazing that the occupying Taleban forces, backed undoubtedly by America, use Islam as an excuse to do the greatest injustice to Afghan women," added the statement.
The Taleban, who captured the Afghan capital Kabul last month, have imposed Islam's stern Sharia law on the city, forbidding women to go to work or continue their education.

Under Iran's Islamic laws, women have to follow a strict dress code and contacts between unmarried men and women are forbidden. But women receive education and are are widely represented in the work force.

Shi'ite Iran recognises the government of Afghan President Burhanuddin Rabbani. Iranian media have accused Pakistan of setting up the Sunni Taleban with backing from the United States, a charge Pakistan denies.
